items.title: Explosions heard in Saudi capital as airport due to reopen
items.summary: Explosions heard in Saudi capital as airport due to reopen AFP RIYADH: Explosions rang out in the Saudi capital on Sunday, as the kingdom was due to reopen Riyadh international airport despite repeated attacks by Yemen's Houthis. Saudi Arabia, which leads a military coalition fighting the Iran-backed Houthis, has faced a barrage of strikes from the group in recent weeks. Riyadh's international airport said flights would resume on Sunday after a two-week closure following the Houthi strikes.

items.title: PN chairman: Does Bersatu still have its heart in PN?
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Perikatan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar has questioned whether Bersatu is still committed to the coalition, citing developments since the Negri Sembilan state election. "With what has happened lately, since the Negri Sembilan election, does Bersatu still its heart in Perikatan Nasional?" We said we invited Bersatu to come to the meeting.

items.title: Mislabelled palm oil blends could hurt Malaysia’s reputation abroad, Maritime experts say
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 25 — Palm oil blended in Malaysia must carry accurate declarations of origin, as any inaccuracy could undermine the integrity and reputation of Malaysian products in international markets, a maritime expert said. Universiti Malaysia Terengganu (UMT) Faculty of Maritime Studies senior lecturer Dr Madzli Harun said that while palm oil blending was permitted in the industry, the process did not automatically make the finished product Malaysian in origin. Madzli said blending alone might not satisfy RoO requirements or change a product’s country of origin, and operators must therefore show that the processing carried out meets the relevant criteria before the finished product can be declared Malaysian in origin.

items.title: Bersatu not the court, emergency PN meeting is compulsory for all parties
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Perikatan Nasional information chief Tan Sri Annuar Musa has criticised Bersatu for questioning the legality of tonight's emergency supreme council meeting, saying the party cannot take over the role of the court. He said the meeting was compulsory as the coalition needed to discuss its preparations for the Melaka election. And Bersatu is not the court.

items.title: Syed Saddiq, Bella's kenduri rakyat swarmed by people since morning
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Even before the event began, crowds had already started streaming into the venue of the kenduri rakyat hosted by Muar member of parliament Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman and his new wife, singer and actress Bella Astillah. Some had been queuing for hours from early morning to ensure they could attend the event, held at the Yong Sheng Banquet Hall in Jalan Bakri, Muar, today. Syed Saddiq and Bella were officially married on Oct 10 in a solemnisation ceremony held at Level 118 of Menara Merdeka 118 here.

items.title: Sanusi: GE16 will be Pakatan’s last term in Putrajaya and Perikatan’s final term as Opposition
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Oct 25 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) election director Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor has predicted that Pakatan Harapan will lose power in Putrajaya at the 16th general election, according to online reports. He told supporters that PN must use the time left before GE16, expected by December 2027, to strengthen its election machinery. According to Sanusi, a PN government would take a new approach to national development, “developing together with Islam”.

items.title: Zahid, national leaders extend congratulations to Sultan of Selangor on silver jubilee
items.summary: In a Facebook post, Ahmad Zahid prayed that Allah would continue to grant Sultan Sharafuddin good health, well-being and strength to continue providing leadership and protection to the people and state of Selangor. “I pray that Allah SWT will continue to grant Your Royal Highness good health, a blessed life and the strength to continue leading and protecting the state and people of Selangor, with wisdom and compassion for all. “May the state of Selangor remain peaceful, prosperous and blessed under Your Royal Highness’ reign.

items.title: No walk-ins: Finas opens RM15m Creative Content Fund applications online only from Nov 16
items.summary: The National Film Development Corporation Malaysia (Finas) said applications would be subject to the prevailing Creative Content Fund guidelines and regulations. The six categories include the International Co-Production Fund for Feature Films/Animated Features, First Time Amateur Film Maker (FAME) Fund and Television Programme Co-Production Fund (Supertelefilm). The other categories are the Micro-Drama Co-Production Fund (Broadcasting Stations/OTT Platforms), Veteran Artists Supertelefilm (STAR) Fund and National Public Service Announcement (PSA) Production Fund.

items.title: Crocodile caught in fisherman's net in Sabah
items.summary: KOTA MARUDU: A fisherman was surprised to find a crocodile caught in his fishing net near Kampung Radu Laut Pangkalan. Kota Marudu Fire and Rescue Station chief Debli Mamoi said: "Upon arrival, the fire and rescue team found a 2m-long crocodile caught in the fishing net," he said. Recently, a 2.8m-long, 100kg crocodile was also found trapped in a fishing net at Kampung Birahan.

items.title: Dzulkefly: MOH strengthening mental health support nationwide, workplace policy under consultation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 25 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) is to continue strengthening the support system and access to mental health services nationwide, including through the development of a mental health policy at the workplace, which is currently undergoing an engagement process with stakeholders. MOH is also expanding access to mental health services through 1,116 government health clinics nationwide, in addition to hospitals and community-based services such as Community Mental Health Centres (MENTARI). “This approach also involves over 500 family medicine specialists who provide mental health services at the primary healthcare level,” he said.

items.title: Fahmi: 2 journalists involved in road accident to get Tabung Kasih@HAWANA aid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Two journalists involved in a road accident in Perak this morning will receive assistance under the Tabung Kasih@HAWANA initiative, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said. He said the Communications Ministry, through the Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama), was arranging assistance for Bernama journalist Nur Afiradina Arshad and New Straits Times (NST) journalist Zahratulhayat Md Arif. -- BERNAMA © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Landslide buries two cars near Tanjung Tokong condo
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: A landslide near Leisure Bay Condominium in Tanjung Tokong this evening partially buried two cars, with no casualties reported. The Penang Fire and Rescue Department received a distress call at 6.50pm. Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director John Sagun Francis said the landslide buried a BMW and a Honda City, both parked nearby.

items.title: Melaka election: Amanah satisfied with five seats, to focus on winning all
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Amanah vice-president Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad says the party is grateful to be contesting five seats in the Melaka election on Nov 14. He said Pakatan Harapan remains united on the seat allocation, adding that Amanah, which has been part of PH since the coalition's formation in 2015, had always acted in tandem with its partners. He said Amanah would now focus on winning all five seats.

items.title: Man found dead outside Cheras food stall; police say no foul play suspected
items.summary: According to The Star , the man was found unconscious at Flat Sri Melaka on Jalan Ikan Emas today, according to Cheras OCPD Asst Comm Mohd Rosdi Daud. An assistant medical officer from Kuala Lumpur Hospital pronounced the man dead at the scene, Mohd Rosdi added. Mohd Rosdi said investigations are ongoing.

items.title: Amanah accepts 5 seats for Melaka polls
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Parti Amanah Negara (Amanah) has accepted Pakatan Harapan's (PH) seat allocation for the Melaka election, despite being allocated five seats compared with nine in the 2021 election. Its vice-president, Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad, said the decision followed thorough negotiations at the coalition's highest level. Under the seat allocation for the Melaka election on Nov 14, PKR will contest nine state seats, DAP seven and Amanah five, bringing the coalition's total to 21 seats.

items.title: Mardi worker killed by bee swarm while collecting honey at farm in Kemaman
items.summary: Kemaman police chief Supt Mohd Razi Rosli said the incident occurred at 9.50am when the victim, Hafizul Mat, 40, a general worker, was at MARDI’s Kemaman branch at Kilometer 18 of Jalan Ayer Putih with a colleague. Mohd Razi said that while in the tree, the victim shouted at his colleague to run as the bees swarmed him. However, Mohd Razi said the hospital confirmed that the victim died while receiving treatment at 6.42pm.

items.title: Workplace mental health policy in final stages, says Dzulkefly
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Health Ministry is finalising a workplace mental health policy. This is after more than 55,000 civil servants were found to be at high risk of mental health issues, including suicidal tendencies. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said engagement sessions with stakeholders were ongoing, and an official announcement would be made once the policy was finalised.

items.title: MetMalaysia warns of thunderstorms, heavy rain in Labuan and six states until 9pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 25 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in Labuan and six states until 9pm tonight. In a statement, MetMalaysia said the areas affected in Kelantan are Pasir Puteh, Bachok, Kota Bharu, Tumpat, Pasir Mas and Machang, while in Pahang, they are Jerantut, Kuantan, Maran, Pekan and Lipis. The warning also covers Terengganu, Johor and Sarawak, including Song in Kapit; Kanowit and Sibu in Sibu; Julau and Pakan in Sarikei; Lubok Antu in Sri Aman; Serian; Betong; and Kuching.

items.title: Pahang Sultan, Tengku Ampuan extend condolences on passing of Kelantan Sultan's aunt
items.summary: KUANTAN: The Sultan of Pahang, Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah, has conveyed his condolences to the Sultan of Kelantan, Sultan Muhammad V, and the Kelantan royal family, following the death of Datuk Tengku Rozan Almarhum Sultan Yahya Petra yesterday. The Tengku Ampuan of Pahang, Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah, also extended her condolences on the passing of the Kelantan Sultan's aunt. Tengku Rozan died at 9.10pm yesterday.

items.title: Haze: 8 areas record unhealthy API readings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Eight areas nationwide recorded unhealthy air quality as of 6pm today, with Serian police headquarters in Sarawak recording the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 192. Unhealthy API readings were also recorded in Terengganu, with Paka registering 156, while Pasir Gudang in Johor recorded 152. Meanwhile, APIMS reported that 50 areas nationwide recorded moderate API readings, while 10 areas remained at the good level.

items.title: Gunung Jerai villages hit by floods repeatedly
items.summary: YAN: Residents of Kampung Titi Teras and Kampung Teroi Bukit at the foot of Gunung Jerai are facing floods again after five hours of continuous heavy rain caused a river to overflow into their homes early today. Kampung Titi Teras Village Community Council chairman Kamarudin Arifin said initial checks found about 20 houses affected by the floods. He said residents grew worried and prepared for possible flooding whenever heavy rain continued.

items.title: GPS needs to continue leading Sarawak to sustain development, says deputy premier
items.summary: KUCHING: Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) must continue to lead the state government to ensure the continuity of socioeconomic development and to keep the future of the people on the right track, said Sarawak Deputy Premier Datuk Awang Tengah Ali Hasan. He urged the people of Sarawak to support GPS in the 13th state election, noting that the current administration has demonstrated a clear direction in driving inclusive progress that encompasses both urban and rural areas. Our choice is the existing government led by the Premier of Sarawak (Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg), the GPS government which has a clear vision to implement transformation and elevate the well-being of the people.

items.title: Haze: Eight areas nationwide record unhealthy API as of 6pm, Serian highest at 192
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 25 — Eight areas nationwide recorded unhealthy air quality as of 6pm today, with Serian IPD in Sarawak recording the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 192. Unhealthy API readings were also recorded in Terengganu, with Paka registering 156, while Pasir Gudang in Johor recorded 152. Meanwhile, APIMS reported that 50 areas nationwide recorded moderate API readings, while 10 areas remained at the good level.

items.title: One psychiatrist per 69,000 people in Malaysia as govt targets improved ratio
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Health Ministry aims to have one psychiatrist for every 40,000 people, compared with the current ratio of one for every 69,000. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the target, aimed at meeting growing demand for mental health services, would be achieved by expanding specialist training. To ease the shortage, Dzulkefly said the ministry was also adopting 'task-shifting', whereby counsellors and family medicine specialists (FMS) take on part of the mental health caseload.

items.title: Police seek dashcam footage, urge witnesses to come forward after crash involving Bernama, NST journalists
items.summary: IPOH, Oct 25 — The police are urging members of the public who witnessed an accident involving a car carrying two journalists and a lorry which occurred this morning on Jalan Ipoh-Lumut, near the Taman Kledang Permai traffic light junction to come forward and assist with the investigation. Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said those who possess dashcam footage of the incident are also requested to provide the information to the Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division of the Ipoh district police headquarters (IPD). He noted that the incident, which took place at approximately 5.45 am., involved a Perodua Bezza carrying the two journalists, who were traveling from the direction of Meru towards Bagan Datuk.

items.title: No piranha found or caught at Klau Dam, but presence not ruled out, says Fisheries Dept
items.summary: KUANTAN, Oct 25 — No piranha fish were found or caught during the Alien Fish Mitigation Programme at the Klau Dam, Raub, which took place over two days starting yesterday, said Fisheries Director-General Datuk Adnan Hussain. He said this mitigation program is one of the inland fisheries management efforts to control alien fish populations and reduce the risk of disruption to native fish species. “No piranha fish were found or caught throughout this program.

items.title: Malaysia, UAE discuss Middle East situation, UN secretary-general nomination
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) exchanged views on current global developments, particularly the ongoing situation in the Middle East, according to a post by Malaysia's Foreign Ministry on the social media platform X on Sunday. The ministry said the discussion took place on Friday during a telephone conversation between Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan and UAE Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Affairs Minister His Highness Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan. Turkiye's national news agency, Anadolu Ajansi, recently reported that Nusseibeh, the UAE's Minister of State and envoy to the UN and the European Union (EU), had announced her candidacy following her formal nomination by the UAE.

items.title: CGS International keeps "Add" call on My DIY
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Mr DIY Group (M) Bhd's exposure to rising e-commerce competition such as China's Pinduoduo free shipping campaign is among the reasons that the stock has been underperforming, according to CGS International. Mr DIY's stock has dropped 24.84 per cent on a year-to-date basis and 33.14 per cent over the past 12 months. It estimated Pinduoduo's Malaysia e-commerce market share at between RM1 billion and RM3 billion per annum or 1.4 to 3.4 per cent, less than 0.4 per cent of Malaysia's total retail sales.

items.title: Man found dead near food stall in Cheras [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A man in his mid-20s was found unconscious and later pronounced dead near a food stall at Flat Sri Melaka, Jalan Ikan Emas, Cheras. Cheras district police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Rosdi Daud said police received a report about the discovery at 9.02am. View on Threads The man was pronounced dead at the scene, Mohd Rosdi said.

items.title: One in 23 Malaysian women now at risk of breast cancer
items.summary: KUCHING: The risk of Malaysian women developing breast cancer has risen to one in 23, compared with one in 27 previously, says Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri. She said that based on the Malaysian National Cancer Registry Report for 2012–2016 and 2017–2021, breast cancer remains the most common cancer among women in the country. She said the programme was later strengthened and rebranded to WeCaRe, which encompasses awareness of breast and cervical cancer among women.

items.title: Haze: Johor schools to reopen in phases, starting with exam candidates
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 25 — Schools in Johor will reopen in phases, with the first phase on Monday (tomorrow) and Tuesday limited to students sitting for examinations according to the scheduled timetable. State Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali said the decision was made following the decree of the Regent of Johor, Tunku Mahkota Ismail, who places great importance on the safety, health and well-being of the people of Johor. Muhammad Naqib said the Johor State Education Department (JPNJ) would coordinate the implementation of health and safety standard operating procedures (SOPs), including the wearing of face masks and monitoring of school activities, based on current air pollutant index (API) readings.

items.title: Haze: Johor schools to reopen in phases, exam candidates first
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Schools in Johor will reopen in phases, with the first phase on tomorrow and Tuesday limited to students sitting for examinations according to the scheduled timetable. State Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali said the decision was made following the decree of the Regent of Johor, Tunku Mahkota Ismail, who places great importance on the safety, health and well-being of the people of Johor. Naqib said the Johor Education Department would coordinate the implementation of health and safety standard operating procedures (SOPs), including the wearing of face masks and monitoring of school activities, based on current air pollutant index (API) readings.

items.title: No piranha found or caught in Klau dam in Raub - Fisheries dept
items.summary: KUANTAN: No piranha fish were found or caught during the Alien Fish Mitigation Programme at the Klau Dam, Raub, which took place over two days starting yesterday, said Fisheries director-general Datuk Adnan Hussain. He said this mitigation program is one of the inland fisheries management efforts to control alien fish populations and reduce the risk of disruption to native fish species. "No piranha fish were found or caught throughout this program.

items.title: Johor expects 26,000 job opportunities for youth this year, says Onn Hafiz
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI, Oct 25 — The Johor government expects 26,000 job opportunities to be offered to young people across the state this year, driven by rapid economic growth and the influx of high-value investments. Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said the projected figure reflected a consistent year-on-year increase, following the success of various strategic initiatives, including the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) and large-scale career events such as the Johor Talent Development Council (JTDC) Mega Job Fair. He said the state had continued to record a significant increase in quality job opportunities compared with previous years.

items.title: [UPDATED] Bersatu warns of legal risks over PN emergency meeting
items.summary: \KUALA LUMPUR: Bersatu has warned that today's emergency Perikatan Nasional (PN) Supreme Council meeting could carry serious legal implications as the coalition's registration has been cancelled. Bersatu secretary-general, Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali, said all parties should preserve the status quo of the Registrar of Societies' decision until all court proceedings had been exhausted. He said that although PN obtained a stay from the High Court on Oct 22, the court had noted that the deregistration had already taken effect.

items.title: Cops nab 6 over restaurant brawl in Lahad Datu
items.summary: LAHAD DATU: Six people, including three women, have been arrested over a fight at a restaurant here believed to have been sparked by jealousy. Lahad Datu district police chief Assistant Commissioner Dzulbaharin Ismail said preliminary investigations indicated that the fight stemmed from jealousy. Dzulbaharin said the case was being investigated under Section 147 of the Penal Code for rioting.

items.title: Four Bangladeshis among six held in Sungai Petani over online gaming scam, syndicate ran from abandoned hotel
items.summary: SUNGAI PETANI, Oct 25 — Police recently arrested six individuals, including four Bangladeshi men, suspected of being involved in an online gaming scam syndicate. Kuala Muda police chief ACP Hanyan Ramlan said the syndicate, which operated from an abandoned hotel in Taman Lagenda near here, was believed to have been active since June. “In a raid at 9.30pm on Wednesday (October 21), a team of officers and personnel from the Kuala Muda District Police Headquarters (IPD) Commercial Crime Investigation Division (CCID) arrested four Bangladeshi men aged between 20 and 53.

items.title: PH-Bersatu cooperation could widen Malay voter reach in Melaka election
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Cooperation with Bersatu could help Pakatan Harapan (PH) reach more Malay voters in next month's Melaka election, but wresting power from Barisan Nasional (BN) will remain difficult. Universiti Malaya senior political science lecturer Dr Mohammad Tawfik Yaakub said PH would need to win 15 of the 28 seats contested, but several factors favoured BN. In the 2021 Melaka state election, PH won five seats, four through DAP and one through Amanah, while PKR failed to win any.

items.title: Man dies after being stung by swarm of bees while collecting honey
items.summary: District police chief Superintendent Mohd Razi Rosli said the victim had asked a 44-year-old friend to accompany him to collect the honey. He said the friend initially told the victim not to take the honey as the tree was very tall, but the victim decided to climb it anyway. "The victim's friend immediately sought ambulance assistance before the victim was rushed to Kemaman Hospital for further treatment," he said.

items.title: 12,500ha of Kelantan padi fields face flood risk during monsoon
items.summary: KOTA BARU: About 12,500 ha of padi fields under the Kemubu Agricultural Development Authority (Kada) scheduled for harvesting in November and December face flood risks during the Northeast Monsoon. Kada chairman Khalid Abdul Samad said 56 per cent of the 25,000 ha of padi cultivation areas under the agency had been harvested for the first season of 2026 as of today. He said Kada implemented five monsoon preparedness measures, including maintaining drainage systems, coordinating water gate operations, operating seven active drainage pumps, scheduling the second padi planting season, and relocating assets to safer areas.

items.title: Melaka polls: PKR’s seven new faces must earn voters’ trust, says Adam Adli
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 25 — Melaka PKR is fielding seven new faces among its nine candidates for next month’s state election, as the party seeks to strengthen support for its reform agenda at the state level. State party acting chairman Adam Adli Abd Halim said PKR needs to work hard to convince voters of the principles and reform agenda it was pursuing at the federal level and ensure they gain acceptance in Melaka. Last night, Prime Minister and Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced the coalition’s 21 candidates for the state election, comprising nine from PKR, seven from DAP and five from Amanah.

items.title: Mah Sing targets 30pct recurring revenue in strategic business shift
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Mah Sing Group Bhd aims to derive 30 per cent of its group revenue from recurring income within the next five years as it diversifies its earnings base beyond property sales and expands its industrial and data centre-related opportunities. Mah Sing founder and group managing director Tan Sri Leong Hoy Kum said recurring income, although currently contributing a relatively small share of revenue, would become an increasingly important part of the group's long-term growth strategy. Its industrial property push includes MS Industrial Park @ Kulai, a RM2.2 billion joint-venture development with KLK Land Sdn Bhd spanning 419.17 acres of freehold land within Zone E of the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ).

items.title: Damaged Kuala Besar jetty puts more than 1,000 users at risk
items.summary: KOTA BARU: More than 1,000 people who travel daily between Kuala Besar and the islands off Tumpat face safety risks due to a badly damaged jetty they rely on to board boats. Damaged by floods last year, the jetty has been left with broken railings and a damaged platform, raising concerns over the safety of residents and visitors travelling to islands including Pulau Suri. "The jetty is our main access point to the islands.

items.title: Haze: 27 schools in Tebedu to close tomorrow, says Sarawak Education Dept
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 25 — Twenty-seven schools in the Tebedu district of Serian will be closed tomorrow due to haze, following continuous monitoring of Air Pollutant Index (API) readings and reports from the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia). The Sarawak State Education Department (JPN) said the Oct 26 closure would involve one secondary school and 26 primary schools under its supervision. The Sarawak JPN said that for schools near districts with API readings exceeding 200, headmasters and principals could consider implementing PdPR by taking into account students’ health and safety.

items.title: IGP: Police identify suspects linked to 1.16-tonne ketamine haul found on Malaysian-owned tanker in Indonesian waters
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 25 — Police have identified several individuals suspected of being linked to the attempted smuggling of 1.16 tonnes of ketamine found aboard a Malaysian-owned tanker in Indonesian waters recently. Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said police were tracking down the individuals and would strive to make arrests as soon as possible, either today or tomorrow. He said the vessel’s decision to turn back and enter Indonesian waters provided the authorities there with an opportunity to conduct investigations and make arrests.

items.title: Fadhlina orders probe, removes Perak principal from school amid harassment allegations
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Oct 25 — Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek has directed the Perak Education Department (JPN) to investigate allegations that a school principal sexually harassed a student. She said the principal has also been temporarily reassigned to the Bagan Datuk District Education Office (PPD) pending the outcome of the investigation, as reported by Harian Metro (HM). The principal has also been placed temporarily at the Bagan Datuk PPD until the investigation is completed,” Fadhlina was quoted as saying.

items.title: FT008 detour near Gua Musang now open to light traffic after sinkhole
items.summary: GUA MUSANG, Oct 25 — A temporary detour at FT008 Section 205.556 along the Gua Musang-Kota Bharu road near the Kesedar Ethnobotanical Recreation Park here was opened to light vehicles at noon today. The detour, which is part of the Central Spine Road (LTU) Project Packages 3B and 3C, is open only to light vehicles. The FT008 federal road near Kesedar Ethnobotanical Recreation Park was closed on Oct 10 following the formation of a sinkhole about eight metres deep.

items.title: Zahid outlines 3 TVET initiatives for rural youth
items.summary: SUNGAI BESAR: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has outlined three technical and vocational education and training (TVET) initiatives to produce skilled workers and entrepreneurs among rural youth. The initiatives are the TVET Premium Career Agreement, TVET Jana Desa and Smart and Green TVET Workshops, which will be implemented in phases. Zahid, who is also rural and regional development minister, said the TVET Premium Career Agreement would prioritise early cooperation with employers in selected programmes, including agreements on competencies, placement conditions and salary packages before trainees are recruited.

items.title: Malaysian woman rescued after falling into 10m-deep hole in Vietnam
items.summary: LAM DONG, Vietnam: A 40-year-old Malaysian woman was rescued after falling into a 10m-deep hole while hiking in Da Lat, Lam Dong, on Sunday, the Vietnam News Agency reported. The incident occurred at 5.45am in the Hon Bo mountain area of Lam Vien-Da Lat ward. Hon Bo Mountain, near Thai Phien flower village in Da Lat, is a popular destination for hiking, cloud hunting, and photography, attracting both residents and tourists.

items.title: Takiyuddin: Bersatu invited to Perikatan talks on RoS case, Melaka polls
items.summary: According to News Straits Times (NST), PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said Bersatu leaders had been invited to attend the meeting at PAS headquarters, but whether they would do so was up to them. He said the allocation of the seven seats assigned to PN for the Melaka polls would also be discussed. He said the limited number of seats available meant PN would need to work out a suitable distribution among the parties involved.

items.title: IGP orders immediate CID probe into Noorizwan’s death in custody
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 25 — Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail has directed the Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) to conduct an immediate investigation into the death of Noorizwan Zulkefly, who died while in police custody at the Cheras District Police Headquarters (IPD). He said the investigation must be conducted thoroughly following the discovery of several unusual injuries on Noorizwan’s body that warranted further scrutiny. However, police were still awaiting the laboratory report to determine the actual cause of Noorizwan’s death, he added.

items.title: Melaka state polls: PKR’s 30pc women candidates offer voters a more inclusive choice, says Fadhlina
items.summary: NIBONG TEBAL, Oct 25 — PKR’s move to field 30 per cent women candidates in the Melaka state election is part of the party’s strategy to offer voters a more inclusive choice, said Wanita PKR chief Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek. She said fielding more women candidates could also strengthen women’s representation in state politics. Yesterday, PH chairman and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced 21 candidates to contest in the Melaka state election.

items.title: A split second, a lifetime of loss: Family recalls fatal Paya Terubong landslide
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Oct 25 — A 73-year-old doctor was killed when a landslide struck his family's home in Taman Seri Rambai, Paya Terubong, trapping him beneath collapsed concrete. The victim, identified as Wong Kar Lin, died when a landslide hit the family’s residence at about 8.36am, trapping him beneath rubble in the kitchen while other family members managed to flee. Poh Lim said only the three of them were at home when the landslide occurred, while the couple’s four children live elsewhere.

items.title: Malaysian hiker rescued after falling into 10m-deep hole in Da Lat, Vietnam
items.summary: LAM DONG (Vietnam), Oct 25 — A 40-year-old Malaysian woman was rescued after falling into a 10m-deep hole while hiking in Da Lat, Lam Dong, today, the Vietnam News Agency (VNA) reported, citing local authorities. The incident occurred at around 5.45am in the Hon Bo mountain area of Lam Vien–Da Lat ward, when the woman, identified by her initials G.S.W., was hiking in the area and fell into a hole, said to be part of an abandoned mining site, about 70cm in diameter. Lam Vien–Da Lat ward coordinated with local forces and the Fire Prevention, Firefighting and Rescue Police Division under the provincial Department of Public Security to aid the tourist.

items.title: Melaka cafe gig death: Police reclassify case as murder after delivery rider dies; 10 detained
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 25 — Police have reclassified the death of a delivery rider who was seriously injured while attending a gig at a cafe in Kampung Jawa here on October 17 as a murder case under Section 302 of the Penal Code. Melaka Tengah police chief ACP Halim Abas said the case was initially investigated under Section 326 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing grievous hurt using a weapon or dangerous object. “On Oct 17, the victim, a 21-year-old man, was seriously injured while at the cafe to watch a gig.

items.title: Fadhlina says RM2,500 allowance for Form Six students to begin in first semester next year
items.summary: NIBONG TEBAL, Oct 25 — Form Six students will receive RM2,500 in living allowances starting from the first semester next year, said Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek. She said the allowances, announced under Budget 2027, would be disbursed after the registration process for all Form Six students had been completed. The amount is equivalent to the allowance received by matriculation students and is expected to benefit 90,000 Form Six students nationwide.

items.title: Trade Ministry puts the squeeze on uncertified squishy toys, seizes over 5,800 nationwide
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 25 — The Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) seized 5,801 squishy toys worth RM70,428 nationwide for failing to display the required Safety Compliance Mark. KPDN Enforcement director-general Datuk Azman Adam said the seizures stemmed from 15 enforcement actions during a Special Inspection on Squishy Toys conducted from October 1 to 14 to ensure compliance with child toy safety standards. “KPDN views child toy safety seriously and will not compromise with any party that fails to comply with regulations under the Consumer Protection Act 1999 (Act 599),” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Grandparents, two grandchildren among four killed after Ford hits stranded tow truck on PLUS near Yong Peng
items.summary: Batu Pahat police chief ACP Shahrulanuar Mushaddat Abdullah Sani said the 5.50pm incident involved a Ford Ranger, a Toyota Vios and a Scania tow truck. “Muhammad Zaharil Hakimie died while receiving treatment at the Parit Yaani Health Clinic,” he said in a statement today. Shahrulanuar said the accident also left four other occupants of the Ford Ranger with severe head injuries, including its driver, Jumie Julong, 35; his wife, Nor Hakimah Zakiah Ab Shukor, 32; and their son, Muhammad Zafrul Hakimie, 3, who are currently receiving treatment in the Yellow Zone of Sultanah Nora Ismail Hospital (HSNI) in Batu Pahat.

items.title: Loke announces RM1,000 payout for Melaka taxi drivers ahead of state polls
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Oct 25 — Transport Minister Anthony Loke today said taxi drivers in Melaka will receive RM1,000 in assistance on Monday, with the aid funded through proceeds from the sale of special “H” vehicle registration numbers. Speaking at Pakatan Harapan's (PH) candidate announcement event in Melaka last night, the DAP secretary-general said the assistance formed part of the federal government's efforts to direct public funds towards initiatives that benefit ordinary Malaysians. Loke said the payment would be funded through proceeds from the sale of special “H” vehicle registration numbers, which raised RM91 million.

items.title: Singapore consulate in Kuching to be located within Kuching South City Council area, says mayor
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 25 — The much-anticipated Consulate-General of Singapore in Kuching will be located within the Kuching South City Council’s (MBKS) jurisdiction, according to Kuching South Mayor Datuk Wee Hong Seng. It is noted that the plan to establish a Consulate-General of Singapore in Kuching was first proposed in 2023. During a courtesy call on Abang Johari in January this year, High Commissioner of Singapore to Malaysia Vanu Gopala Menon announced that Singapore intended to set up consulates in both Kuching and Kota Kinabalu to enhance connections in trade, investment and tourism.
